chapter: The Second Herd and its sidemen
title: Harris's practical jokes: dummies in the trombone section
summary: Harris and Red Norvo had life-size dummies, one sat in the trombone section; other pranks including the elevator and stage cleats.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: And he loved to rib people. He had a wild sense of humor. Everything from slapstick to more sophisticated levels. But it's -- he was a very funny man and a very kind and warm man. Well, some of his better escapades was having life-size dummies in the trombone section.

He and Red Norvo wound up with these two lifesize dummies which were part of an act. Some people they'd run across, and there were a dancer who worked with these dummies. So they outfitted -- well, at least, Bill, the one he ended up with, he outfitted him with another band uniform. And he had him sitting next to him in the trombone section, with a horn propped there. And argued with him all night on the stand.
"Man, I told you to come in."
Oh, that's funny. Those are good things to recall.
You have other things like that? I'm sure there's a potful of them.
Yeah, oh, I know. Well, in his more milder moments, he'd get in an elevator and -- in Chicago one

one day, he dropped his pants as he was leaving. He loved that kind of humor. And at one point, he had me calling some guy who was no longer -- evidently was not still around, but he was a man in Philadelphia who he had heard about, who had originally made cleats that went into the stages, and you could buy these shoes that comics would get, big shoes and they'd fit into the cleats and you could lean forward or lean back, or make some wild moves.
And I tried desperately for months to find this guy to make him a set of cleats. And he had it all worked out, how he was going to play //Everywhere// or something, and do that.
